name: Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome with Periventricular Heterotopia
aliases: Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome and Periventricular Nodular Heterotopia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for EDS with Periventricular Heterotopia

criteria.description: Generalized skin hyperextensibility and joint hypermobility consistent with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
Presence of periventricular nodular heterotopia confirmed by brain MRI
Family history of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome or periventricular heterotopia
Evidence of vascular fragility such as easy bruising or arterial rupture

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both major criteria (connective tissue abnormalities and periventricular heterotopia on MRI) with or without minor/supportive criteria
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including clinical, imaging, and genetic assessment.

pathognomonic.notes: Detected by MRI as ectopic gray matter nodules along lateral ventricles
Assessed by Beighton score or equivalent

common.notes: May be related to structural brain abnormalities

occasional.notes: Due to cortical malformations associated with heterotopia
Common valvular abnormality in connective tissue disorders
Reduced muscle tone contributing to joint instability

rare.notes: Severe vascular complication requiring urgent intervention
Mild intellectual disability reported in some cases
Manifesting as constipation or delayed gastric emptying

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible mild anemia secondary to bruising
imaging: Brain MRI showing periventricular nodular heterotopia
Echocardiogram revealing mitral valve prolapse or arterial abnormalities
genetic: Mutations in FLNA gene associated with periventricular heterotopia
Variants in collagen-related genes linked to Ehlers-Danlos syndrome features
other: Beighton score assessment for joint hypermobility

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of periventricular heterotopia on brain imaging
More prominent skin fragility and scarring
Neurological symptoms without connective tissue abnormalities
Typically no joint hypermobility or skin hyperextensibility
Arterial tortuosity and aneurysms with craniofacial features
Distinct genetic mutations (TGFBR1/2) and absence of periventricular heterotopia

redFlags: Sudden onset severe headache or neurological deficit indicating possible vascular rupture
Progressive joint dislocations or severe skin tearing
references: Orphanet: Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome with Periventricular Heterotopia, ORPHA:82004
Sheen, V. L., et al. (2005). Filamin A mutations cause periventricular heterotopia with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome. Neurology.
Malfait, F., et al. (2017). The 2017 international classification of the Ehlers-Danlos syndromes. American Journal of Medical Genetics Part C.
